a: कार्तवीर्यः — The son of Kṛtavīrya and king of the Haihayas, who ruled at Māhiṣmatī. [Having worshipped Dattātreya, he obtained from him several boons, such as a thousand arms, a golden chariot that went wheresoever he willed it to go, the power of restraining wrong by justice, conquest of earth, invincibility by enemies &c.; (cf. R. 6. 39). According to the Vāyu Purāṇa he ruled justly and righteously for 85000 years and offered 10000 sacrifices. He was a contemporary of Ravaṇa whom he once captured and confined like a beast in a corner of his city; cf. R. 6. 40. Kārtavīrya was slain by Paraśurāma for having carried off by violence the Kāmadhenu of his revered father Jamadagni. Kārtavīrya is also known by the name Sahasrārjuna.].

a: कार्तिकेयः — [कृत्तिकानामपत्यं ढक्] N. of Skanda (so called because he was reared by the six Kṛttikās). [Kārtikeya is the Mars or the god of war of the Indian mythology. He is the son of Śiva (but born without the direct intervention of a woman). Most of his epithets have reference to the circumstances of his birth. Śiva cast his seed into Agni (who had gone to the god in the form of a dove while he was enjoying Pārvatī's company), who being unable to bear it cast it into the Ganges; (hence Skanda is called Agnibhū, Gaṅgāputra). It was then transferred to the six Kṛttikās (when they went to bathe in the Ganges), each of whom therefore conceived and brought forth a son. But these six sons were afterwards mysteriously combined into one of extraordinary form with six heads and twelve hands and eyes, (hence he is called Kārtikeya, Shadānana, Ṣaṇmukha &c.). According to another account the seed of Śiva was cast by the Ganges into a thicket of reeds (Śara); whence the boy was called Śaravaṇabhava, or Śarajanman. He is said to have pierced the mountain Krauncha, whence his name Krauñcadāraṇa. He was the commander of the army of the gods in their war with Tāraka, a powerful demon q. v. whom he vanquished and slew; and hence his names Senānī and Tārakajit. He is represented as riding a peacock.] --Comp. --प्रसूः f. Pārvatī, mother of Kārtikeya.

tvAM namAmi sureSvara!” । kASIsvaRqe “vratinaH kArtike mAsi snAtasya viDivan mama । dAmodara! gfhARArDyaM danujendranisUdana! nitye nEmittike kftsne kArtike pApaSozaRe । gfhARArDyaM mayA dattaM rADayA sahito hare!” । iti । pAdme tilErAlipya dehaM svaM nAmoccAraRapUrvakam । snAtvA tu viDinA sanDyAmupAsya gfhamAbrajet । upalipyATa devAgre nirmAya svastikaM praBum । tulasImAlatI padmAgastyapuzpAdinArcayet । nityaM vEzRavasaNgatyA seveta BagavatkaTAm । sarpizAharniSaM dIpaM tilatElena cArccayet । viSezataSca nEvedyAnyarpayedAcarettaTA । praRAmAMSca yaTASakti ekaBaktAdikaM vratam” । pAdme'nyatra “prAtarutTAya SOcAdi kftvA gatvA jalASayam । kftvA ca viDivat snAnaM tato dAmIdarArccanam” । kiYca “mOnena BojanaM kAryaM kArttike vrataDAriRA । Gftena dIpadAnaM syAt tilatElena vA punaH । dinaYca kfzRakaTayA vEzRavAnAM ca saNgamEH । nIyatAM kArtike mAsi maNkalpavratapAlanam । ASvine Suklalakzasya prAramBo harivAsare । aTa vA pOrRamAsItaH saMkrAntO vA tulAgame । dIpadAnamaKaRqaYca dadyAdvE vizRusanniDO । devAlaye tulasyAM vA AkASe vA taduttamam” । kiYca “rajataM kanakaM dIpAn maRimuktAPalAdikam । dAmodarasya prItyarTaM pradadyAt kArtike naraH” । skAnde ca “na gfhe kArtike kuryyAdveSezeRa tu kArtikom । tIrTetu kArtikIM kuryyAt sarvayatnena BAvini!” । kArtike varjyAni skAnde brahmanAradasaMvAde “kArtike tu viSezeRa rAjamAzAMSca Bakzayan । nizpAvAn muniSArdUla! yAvadAhUtanArakI । kaliNgAni pawolAni vfntAkaM sanDitAni ca । na tyajet kArtike mAsi yAvadAhUtanArakI । kArtike mAsi DarmAtmA matsyamAMsaM na Bakzayet । tatrEva yatnatastyAjya SASakaM SOkaraM taTA” । kiYca--parAnnaM paraSayyAYca prarIvAdaM parANganAm । sarvadA varjjayet prAjYo viSezeRa tu kArtike । tElAByaNgaM taTA SayyAM parAnnaM kAMsyaBojanam । kArttike varjjayedyastu paripUrRabratI Bavet । saMprAptaM kArttikaM dfzwvA parAnnaM yastu varjjayet । dine dine tu kfcCasya PalaM prApnoti mAnavaH” । tatrEva SrIrukyANgadamohinIsaMvAde “kArttike varjjayenmaDu । kArttike varjjayet kAMsyaM kArttike SuktasanDitam । na matsyaM BakzayenmAMsaM na kOrmmaM nAnyadeva hi । cARqAlaH sa Bavet suBru! m: कार्त्तिकेय m. N. of a son of Śiva and Pārvatī (popularly regarded as god of war, because he leads the Gaṇas or hosts of Śiva against the demon hosts See RTL. p. 213; accord. to one legend he was son of Śiva without the intervention of Pārvatī, the generative energy of Śiva being cast into the fire and then received by the Ganges, whence he is sometimes described as son of Agni and Gaṅgā; when born he was fostered by the six Kṛttikās q.v., and these offering their six breasts to the child he became six-headed; he is also called Kumāra, Skanda, and Subrahmaṇya; his N. Kārttikeya may be derived from his foster mothers or from the month Kārttika as the best for warfare: in the Mṛcch. and elsewhere he is regarded as presiding over thieves), MBh. &c.
